description:
FILED s456af.  The `symref` bench row regressed 34% PCL-side between 2026-08-25 (par.0.1, 0.1601s) and now (0.2155s) while perl held at 0.021s -- a REAL regression, distinguished from the load noise on `ovlsub` only by reading the ABSOLUTE pcl seconds instead of the pcl/perl ratio (that reading rule is now par.0.2a).  BISECTED commit by commit (BENCH_K=3 per commit; the row is ${'main::g'} + ${'g'} + scalar(@{'main::ga'}) in a 200k loop): 99b003d 0.1578 -> 91633d6 0.1739 (#525, an unqualified symbolic name resolves in the perl-level current package, +10%) -> c8a8311 0.1737 -> f937afd 0.1804 -> 80a11a7 0.1844 -> 7ca3da4 0.2150 (#685, a foreign-qualified symbolic name never reaches main's magic, +16.6%) -> 0dd7434 0.2247 -> 83b335f 0.2155.  So it is NOT a bug and NOT a mystery: it is the accumulated price of the round-5-10 correctness work on the symbolic-name resolver, two thirds of it in the two commits that made resolution package-aware.  NOTHING SHOULD BE REVERTED.  The question this task carries is whether any of it is recoverable without losing the correctness: the resolver now does per-ACCESS package lookup where it used to do less, so the candidate is a per-call-site memo on the resolved cell.  DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT TO TAKE FIRST (do not skip it, the s335 rule): sb-sprof the symref bench and report what fraction is the package lookup vs the cell read -- if the lookup is not dominant there is no task here.  Invalidation is the same blocker #582 has (a package/@ISA/glob write must invalidate), so read #582 before designing.  Priority: LOW -- symbolic refs are not a hot idiom in real code; this is filed so the number is explained rather than re-derived.
s459am: NOT MEASURED â the session's budget went to #862 ARM A (which needed
the full sweep, a two-population gate-set scan and the artifacts) and to #814.
Recording that explicitly rather than leaving it ambiguous, per the s335 rule:
the discriminating measurement this task names (sb-sprof the symref bench and
report what fraction is the package lookup vs the cell read) is STILL THE
FIRST THING TO DO, and it is still cheap.  Nothing here was implemented and
nothing was ruled out.
One datum from s459am's bench runs, for whoever takes it: the `symref` row
read 0.2175 s / 9.75x on this machine at e9296cb, consistent with the 0.2155 s
this task bisected to â so the regression has not drifted further and the
number in the task body is still the live one.

======================================================================
THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, TAKEN (s460ao, agent AO, round 17).
And the answer is NEITHER of the two things this task asked about.
======================================================================

sb-sprof, :cpu mode, 0.5 ms interval, the bench's own program at n=2,000,000
(2008 samples over 1.004 s; reproduced twice, rows stable).  Flat profile,
grouped:

  %p-symref-symbol  (the whole NAME -> SYMBOL resolution)  ..... 87.2 % total
    of which, the PACKAGE / SYMBOL LOOKUP proper:
      %get-package 4.3, %find-symbol 5.1, find-package 0.8,
      find-symbol 0.8                                     ..... ~11 %
    of which, STRING WORK ON THE NAME:
      search 34.3 (finding "::"), %pcl-invert-case 20.3,
      upper-case-p 7.0 + lower-case-p 3.9 + string-upcase 4.4,
      %concatenate-to-string 8.2, vector-subseq 4.3,
      %pcl-non-ascii-name-p 2.0                           ..... ~76 %
  unbox  (THE CELL READ)                                  ..... 0.5 %

So: **the package lookup is NOT dominant (~11 %), the cell read is noise
(0.5 %), and ~76 % of the row is mangling the NAME STRING** — splitting
"main::g" on "::", inverting case, upcasing, concatenating — once per access,
2M times, for a string that is a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT at every one of these
call sites.

WHY THAT RETARGETS THE TASK.  The candidate this task named was "a per-call-
site memo on the resolved CELL", and it correctly noted that #582's
invalidation blocker applies: a package / @ISA / glob write must invalidate a
cached cell.  **But the 76 % does not need that memo at all.**  Caching
name -> SYMBOL is a different question from caching name -> CELL: the symbol
for a given (name string, current perl package) pair is STABLE FOREVER — a
later `*main::g = ...` rebinds what the symbol HOLDS, which is exactly what
the cell read then picks up.  So an `equal` memo keyed on (name,
current-package) inside %p-symref-symbol has NO invalidation blocker, and it
sits in front of ~76 % of this row while leaving every semantic the round-5-10
correctness work established (#525's current-package resolution stays in the
KEY; #685's foreign-qualified rule is upstream of the mangling).

Read #582 before touching the CELL half; it does not gate the SYMBOL half.

SIZE, from the same profile: killing the string work would take the row from
0.2155 s toward ~0.06 s, i.e. from ~9.8x perl to ~2.5x.  That is the whole
regression this task was filed to explain, and more.  Still LOW priority by
the task's own reasoning (symbolic refs are not a hot idiom), but it is now a
sized, unblocked, runtime-only change rather than an open question.

NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE — s460ao's brief was the measurement only.


SHIPPED s461aq (round 18).  `%p-symref-symbol` is a memo wrapper over the old
body (`%p-symref-symbol-uncached`): an `equal` table keyed on the NAME STRING
whose value is a list of #(sigil-char current-package-string symbol), so one
string hash replaces the five string walks and three allocations sb-sprof
measured as ~76 % of the row.  Only a HIT is stored (a miss must stay a miss
or `${"n"} = 1; ${"n"}` keeps answering undef); a CREATE hit still runs
%p-ensure-storage (an entry may have been stored by a READER, which never
gives the symbol its cell); stored keys go through %pcl-memo-key.  NO
invalidation is needed â the answer is which SYMBOL a name denotes, which is
stable forever, and the only operation that changes it is `shadow`, performed
at exactly one site (%p-symref-intern), which clrhashes.

MEASURED (tools/bench-exec.pl BENCH_K=3, both trees, machine quiet):
    symref  0.3644 s / 10.59x  ->  0.0384 s / 1.43x     (9.5x faster)
That beats the ~0.06 s / ~2.5x the task predicted.  Probed vs perl 5.40.3:
the #525 family (unqualified resolution from two packages, ${"X::v"} /
${"main::v"} / ${"::v"}, read-before-create, the same bare name read
alternately from two packages) and the #685 family (%{"foo::ENV"} stays
separate, ${"1"} after a match, @{"main::ga"} vs @{"ga"}) â byte-identical.
Bars: gate PASS 191/6462, full sweep GATE clean TOTAL 18342 (+0) drops 5 =
census, gate-SET scan 638x2 IDENTICAL, companion op/ leg zero real movers.
subject: symref bench: the cost is NEITHER the package lookup (~11%) NOR the cell read (0.5%) -- it is ~76% NAME-STRING MANGLING per access; a name->SYMBOL memo has no #582 invalidation blocker (measured s460ao)
